upstream.title: Endpoint Anticipation for Low-Latency Spoken Dialogue

source_observations.mechanism: speech-based proactive forecasting of end-of-turn signals before the actual endpoint, enabling speculative downstream execution on partial context
source_observations.reported_baseline_relation: authors report consistent gains over competitive VAP-based baselines across conversational and task-oriented datasets

relationship_to_existing_f2_candidates.pipecat_smart_turn_v3_2: primarily a reactive semantic EOT classifier after a pause; Endpoint Anticipation instead forecasts the endpoint before it occurs
relationship_to_existing_f2_candidates.next_turn_duration_aware_endpointing: predicts time-to-next-speech-onset / pause duration behavior; Endpoint Anticipation is a proactive latency-hiding trigger for speculative downstream work
relationship_to_existing_f2_candidates.dualturn: broader interaction-state / two-channel turn-taking research; Endpoint Anticipation can be evaluated as a narrow speculative-start signal rather than as the sole turn controller

f2_architecture_delta.candidate_role: non-authoritative speculative-start signal upstream of committed response generation
safe_composition: Endpoint Anticipation may start a cancellable speculative LLM branch on partial context
optional TTS preflight may prepare but must not make unconfirmed audio canonical/spoken
VoiceIntent/GWT/turn-controller confirmation remains the response-commit gate
barge-in, resumed user speech or changed transcript cancels the speculative branch
unheard text/audio must never be recorded as spoken in VoiceOutcome or UnifiedDB

hypothesis: A proactive endpoint-anticipation signal can hide part of local LLM/TTS sequential latency without weakening Frankenstein's deterministic turn/cancellation authority, if speculative work remains uncommitted and fully cancellable.
counterhypotheses: The reported 28.4% speculative-compute overhead may create CPU/GPU contention on clay-direct-dev and erase the latency benefit for a fully local stack.
Forecast errors on German hesitation, clause-final prosody, self-repair and backchannels may increase wasted generation and cancellation churn.
A strong reactive German Smart Turn / Next-Turn controller plus faster ASR/TTS may already achieve the same perceived latency with less resource complexity.
Starting TTS too early risks semantic/audio commit errors unless audible playback remains behind an explicit commit fence.

recommended_measurement.common_corpus: same pinned German room-audio turns used by the Trigger-7 turn-controller benchmark
metrics: user-speech-end to first audible Frankenstein audio
